dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you please describe the new movements you have been experiencing and when they first started?

Doctor, I just can't seem to sit still anymore; I feel this constant, internal restlessness that forces me to keep moving. It started a few weeks after I began the new medication, and now I'm always pacing or crossing and uncrossing my legs.
I understand that restlessness can be very distressing. What is the name of the new medication you started, and what condition was it prescribed for?

I’m taking risperidone, which my doctor prescribed because I was having some trouble with paranoid thoughts and hearing things. It has actually helped a lot with those symptoms, but now I just can't stop fidgeting.
Have you noticed any other involuntary movements, such as in your face, tongue, or hands? REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination

RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature: 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure: 120/80 mmHg, Heart Rate: 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate: 14 breaths/min; Neurological Examination: Mental Status: Alert and oriented, improved psychotic symptoms. Cranial Nerves: Intact. Motor: Normal tone and strength, no involuntary movements. Sensory: Intact. Coordination: Normal. Gait: Normal, but exhibits inability to sit still with frequent pacing.
Besides the physical need to move, do you feel an intense sense of inner tension or anxiety? How has this restlessness impacted your ability to sleep at night?

It definitely feels like a constant inner tension that I just can't shake unless I'm moving. It's making it really hard to sleep because as soon as I lie down, I feel like I need to get up and pace the room.
Are you taking any other medications, supplements, or consuming high amounts of caffeine that might be contributing to this feeling? Also, has the dose of your risperidone changed recently?

I’m not taking anything else or any supplements, and I don't really drink much caffeine since I mostly stick to water. My doctor did increase my risperidone dose about three weeks ago, right around the time this constant need to move became unbearable.
I've noted that the dose increase correlates with the onset of your symptoms. Do you experience any muscle stiffness, cramping, or a feeling that your muscles are "stuck" in one position?
No, I haven't noticed any stiffness or my muscles getting stuck like that. It’s really just this overwhelming urge to keep moving my legs and pacing around the room.

Do you experience any unusual sensations in your legs, like a "creepy-crawly" or tingling feeling, particularly when you are trying to rest? Have you ever had symptoms like this before starting psychiatric medications?

No, I don't have any tingling or "creepy-crawly" feelings in my legs; it's just a pure, intense need to move. I’ve never experienced anything like this before I started taking these psychiatric medications.
It sounds like you are experiencing a common side effect of your medication called akathisia, which is characterized by that intense inner restlessness and need to move. Since your symptoms began and

I'm relieved to finally have a name for this, but is there anything we can do to make it stop? I really want to keep taking the medicine since it helps my head, but I can't live with this constant need to pace.
I understand how frustrating this is, and we can certainly look into adjusting your dose or adding a medication like a beta-blocker to help. Before we proceed, have these feelings ever become so

No, it hasn't gotten to that point, but the restlessness is definitely exhausting me. I just want to feel calm and still again without those old thoughts coming back. What are the next steps for us to try?

We will work closely with your psychiatrist to manage this by either lowering the risperidone dose or adding a medication like propranolol. I have enough information to confirm that this is a side effect of your

That sounds like a good plan, because I'm really tired of feeling like I'm constantly "on the go." If we try the propranolol or change the dose, how long does it usually take for this restless feeling to finally go away? I'm just looking forward to being able to sit through a whole class without needing to get up and pace.

With treatment or a dose adjustment, you should start to feel relief within a few days. I'm glad we caught this early so we can get you back to feeling comfortable and focused.

DI

That’s such a relief to hear because I’ve been worried I’d have to choose between my sanity and being able to sit still. Thank you, Doctor, I’m ready to try whatever you think is best so I can finally just relax. I'll make sure to keep a close eye on how I'm feeling once we make the changes.

You're very welcome, and we will get this sorted out right away. Please reach out if you have any further concerns as we adjust your treatment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Akath
